title: Keyword argument before variable positional arguments list in the definition of … function.
summary: When defining a keyword argument before variable positional arguments, one can end up in having multiple values passed for the aforementioned parameter in case the method is called with keyword arguments. pylint calls it keyword-arg-before-vararg.
message_templates: Keyword argument before variable positional arguments list in the definition of {} function

title: Positional arguments appear to be out of order.
summary: Emitted when the caller's argument names fully match the parameter names in the function signature but do not have the same order. pylint calls it arguments-out-of-order.
message_templates: Positional arguments appear to be out of order

title: Non-string value assigned to __name__.
summary: Emitted when a non-string value is assigned to __name__. pylint calls it non-str-assignment-to-dunder-name.
message_templates: Non-string value assigned to __name__

title: Second argument of isinstance is not a type.
summary: Emitted when the second argument of an isinstance call is not a type. pylint calls it isinstance-second-argument-not-valid-type.
message_templates: Second argument of isinstance is not a type

title: … will be included in … since a positional-only parameter with this name already exists.
summary: Emitted when a function is called with a keyword argument that has the same name as a positional-only parameter and the function contains a keyword variadic parameter dict. pylint calls it kwarg-superseded-by-positional-arg.
message_templates: {} will be included in {} since a positional-only parameter with this name already exists

title: Use … formatting in logging functions.
summary: Used when a logging statement has a call form of "logging.<logging method>(format_string % (format_args...))". Use another type of string formatting instead. You can use % formatting but leave interpolation to the logging function by passing the parameters as arguments. If logging-fstring-interpolation is disabled then you can use fstring formatting. If logging-format-interpolation is disabled then you can use str.format. pylint calls it logging-not-lazy.
message_templates: Use {} formatting in logging functions

title: Use … formatting in logging functions.
summary: Used when a logging statement has a call form of "logging.<logging method>(format_string.format(format_args...))". Use another type of string formatting instead. You can use % formatting but leave interpolation to the logging function by passing the parameters as arguments. If logging-fstring-interpolation is disabled then you can use fstring formatting. If logging-not-lazy is disabled then you can use % formatting as normal. pylint calls it logging-format-interpolation.
message_templates: Use {} formatting in logging functions

title: Use … formatting in logging functions.
summary: Used when a logging statement has a call form of "logging.<logging method>(f"...")".Use another type of string formatting instead. You can use % formatting but leave interpolation to the logging function by passing the parameters as arguments. If logging-format-interpolation is disabled then you can use str.format. If logging-not-lazy is disabled then you can use % formatting as normal. pylint calls it logging-fstring-interpolation.
message_templates: Use {} formatting in logging functions

title: Format string dictionary key should be a string, not ….
summary: Used when a format string that uses named conversion specifiers is used with a dictionary whose keys are not all strings. pylint calls it bad-format-string-key.
message_templates: Format string dictionary key should be a string, not {}

title: Unused key … in format string dictionary.
summary: Used when a format string that uses named conversion specifiers is used with a dictionary that contains keys not required by the format string. pylint calls it unused-format-string-key.
message_templates: Unused key {} in format string dictionary

title: Invalid format string.
summary: Used when a PEP 3101 format string is invalid. pylint calls it bad-format-string.
message_templates: Invalid format string

title: Missing keyword argument … for format string.
summary: Used when a PEP 3101 format string that uses named fields doesn't receive one or more required keywords. pylint calls it missing-format-argument-key.
message_templates: Missing keyword argument {} for format string

title: Unused format argument ….
summary: Used when a PEP 3101 format string that uses named fields is used with an argument that is not required by the format string. pylint calls it unused-format-string-argument.
message_templates: Unused format argument {}

title: Format string contains both automatic field numbering and manual field specification.
summary: Used when a PEP 3101 format string contains both automatic field numbering (e.g. '{}') and manual field specification (e.g. '{0}'). pylint calls it format-combined-specification.
message_templates: Format string contains both automatic field numbering and manual field specification

title: Missing format attribute … in format specifier ….
summary: Used when a PEP 3101 format string uses an attribute specifier ({0.length}), but the argument passed for formatting doesn't have that attribute. pylint calls it missing-format-attribute.
message_templates: Missing format attribute {} in format specifier {}

title: Using invalid lookup key … in format specifier ….
summary: Used when a PEP 3101 format string uses a lookup specifier ({a[1]}), but the argument passed for formatting doesn't contain or doesn't have that key as an attribute. pylint calls it invalid-format-index.
message_templates: Using invalid lookup key {} in format specifier {}

title: Duplicate string formatting argument …, consider passing as named argument.
summary: Used when we detect that a string formatting is repeating an argument instead of using named string arguments. pylint calls it duplicate-string-formatting-argument.
message_templates: Duplicate string formatting argument {}, consider passing as named argument

title: Using an f-string that does not have any interpolated variables.
summary: Used when we detect an f-string that does not use any interpolation variables, in which case it can be either a normal string or a bug in the code. pylint calls it f-string-without-interpolation.
message_templates: Using an f-string that does not have any interpolated variables

title: Using formatting for a string that does not have any interpolated variables.
summary: Used when we detect a string that does not have any interpolation variables, in which case it can be either a normal string without formatting or a bug in the code. pylint calls it format-string-without-interpolation.
message_templates: Using formatting for a string that does not have any interpolated variables

title: Anomalous backslash in string: '…'. String constant might be missing an r prefix.
summary: Used when a backslash is in a literal string but not as an escape. pylint calls it anomalous-backslash-in-string.
message_templates: Anomalous backslash in string: '{}'. String constant might be missing an r prefix.

title: Anomalous Unicode escape in byte string: '…'. String constant might be missing an r or u prefix.
summary: Used when an escape like \\u is encountered in a byte string where it has no effect. pylint calls it anomalous-unicode-escape-in-string.
message_templates: Anomalous Unicode escape in byte string: '{}'. String constant might be missing an r or u prefix.

title: Implicit string concatenation found in ….
summary: String literals are implicitly concatenated in a literal iterable definition : maybe a comma is missing ?. pylint calls it implicit-str-concat.
message_templates: Implicit string concatenation found in {}

title: Quote delimiter … is inconsistent with the rest of the file.
summary: Quote delimiters are not used consistently throughout a module (with allowances made for avoiding unnecessary escaping). pylint calls it inconsistent-quotes.
message_templates: Quote delimiter {} is inconsistent with the rest of the file

title: The u prefix for strings is no longer necessary in Python >=3.0.
summary: Used when we detect a string with a u prefix. These prefixes were necessary in Python 2 to indicate a string was Unicode, but since Python 3.0 strings are Unicode by default. pylint calls it redundant-u-string-prefix.
message_templates: The u prefix for strings is no longer necessary in Python >=3.0

title: "…" is not a valid mode for open.
summary: Python supports: r, w, a[, x] modes with b, +, and U (only with r) options. See https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#open. pylint calls it bad-open-mode.
message_templates: "{}" is not a valid mode for open.

title: Using datetime.time in a boolean context.
summary: Using datetime.time in a boolean context can hide subtle bugs when the time they represent matches midnight UTC. This behaviour was fixed in Python 3.5. See https://bugs.python.org/issue13936 for reference. This message can't be emitted when using Python >= 3.5. pylint calls it boolean-datetime.
message_templates: Using datetime.time in a boolean context.

title: Redundant use of … with constant value ….
summary: The first argument of assertTrue and assertFalse is a condition. If a constant is passed as parameter, that condition will be always true. In this case a warning should be emitted. The same applies to assertEqual and assertNotEqual when both compared values are constants. pylint calls it redundant-unittest-assert.
message_templates: Redundant use of {} with constant value {}

title: Threading.Thread needs the target function.
summary: The warning is emitted when a threading.Thread class is instantiated without the target function being passed as a kwarg or as a second argument. By default, the first parameter is the group param, not the target param. pylint calls it bad-thread-instantiation.
message_templates: threading.Thread needs the target function

title: Using copy.copy(os.environ). Use os.environ.copy() instead.
summary: Os.environ is not a dict object but proxy object, so shallow copy has still effects on original object. See https://bugs.python.org/issue15373 for reference. pylint calls it shallow-copy-environ.
message_templates: Using copy.copy(os.environ). Use os.environ.copy() instead.

title: … default type is …. Expected str or None.
summary: Env manipulation functions return None or str values. Supplying anything different as a default may cause bugs. See https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.html#os.getenv. pylint calls it invalid-envvar-default.
message_templates: {} default type is {}. Expected str or None.

title: Using preexec_fn keyword which may be unsafe in the presence of threads.
summary: The preexec_fn parameter is not safe to use in the presence of threads in your application. The child process could deadlock before exec is called. If you must use it, keep it trivial! Minimize the number of libraries you call into. See https://docs.python.org/3/library/subprocess.html#popen-constructor. pylint calls it subprocess-popen-preexec-fn.
message_templates: Using preexec_fn keyword which may be unsafe in the presence of threads

title: 'subprocess.run' used without explicitly defining the value for 'check'.
summary: The check keyword is set to False by default. It means the process launched by subprocess.run can exit with a non-zero exit code and fail silently. It's better to set it explicitly to make clear what the error-handling behavior is. pylint calls it subprocess-run-check.
message_templates: 'subprocess.run' used without explicitly defining the value for 'check'.

title: Using open without explicitly specifying an encoding.
summary: It is better to specify an encoding when opening documents. Using the system default implicitly can create problems on other operating systems. See https://peps.python.org/pep-0597/ This message can't be emitted when using Python >= 3.15. pylint calls it unspecified-encoding.
message_templates: Using open without explicitly specifying an encoding

title: Leaving functions creating breakpoints in production code is not recommended.
summary: Calls to breakpoint(), sys.breakpointhook() and pdb.set_trace() should be removed from code that is not actively being debugged. pylint calls it forgotten-debug-statement.
message_templates: Leaving functions creating breakpoints in production code is not recommended

title: 'lru_cache(maxsize=None)' or 'cache' will keep all method args alive indefinitely, including 'self'.
summary: By decorating a method with lru_cache or cache the 'self' argument will be linked to the function and therefore never garbage collected. Unless your instance will never need to be garbage collected (singleton) it is recommended to refactor code to avoid this pattern or add a maxsize to the cache. The default value for maxsize is 128. pylint calls it method-cache-max-size-none.
message_templates: 'lru_cache(maxsize=None)' or 'cache' will keep all method args alive indefinitely, including 'self'

title: Checks for indentation that uses tabs.
summary: According to PEP 8, spaces are preferred over tabs (unless used to remain consistent with code that is already indented with tabs). Ruff takes this rule from pycodestyle and made it stable in v0.0.254.
message_templates: Indentation contains tabs
